text:
anna: Quick heads-up — planning a slim-shift from router0 -> router1 tomorrow 02:00 UTC. 3-step: 10% / 50% / 100%, 10m probes between steps. Keeping a 30m grace window for canary rollback.
kevin: sounds good. what's pinned? release notes? :eyes:
sara: We should pin image v2.3.1 and the routing config version `rtr-2026-03-slim`.
anna: yes pinning `service:v2.3.1` and config `rtr-2026-03-slim`. I'll attach a short release note in the deploy description.
chris: can we add a quick perf probe on p95 and model-load errors? want to ensure no mem spikes.
anna: good call. will add `p95_latency` and `kv_cache_miss` to probes.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: router-weighted-shift by @anna
deploy-bot: steps: 1) apply routing patch, 2) slow-drain warmup on router1, 3) shift weights 10/50/100, 4) validate probes, 5) mark complete.
ops-bot: FYI — scheduled maintenance window recorded: 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z -> 2026-03-22T03:00:00Z
kevin: release notes draft: "Slimshift: make router1 handle bulk traffic for lower p95 and better tail isolation. Pinned service:v2.3.1. Rollback plan included." Short enough?
sara: perfect. add a note about fallback policy: automatic fallback to router0 on probe failure or >3% user errors in 5m.
chris: what are the exact thresholds? need them in the deploy bot config.
anna: thresholds: p95 increase >20% over baseline OR error_rate >3% sustained over 5m OR CPU >85% on router1 for 2 consecutive 2m samples.
kevin: ok added to the deploy description. Also added a manual abort step — @chris or @sara can send `abort-shift` to stop and pin back to router0.
sara: can we test the abort command in staging first? last time the command had flaky permission.
chris: tested in staging yesterday, works for me. permission: infra group + release-approvers.
anna: approvals: need two approvers for change window. @kevin and @sara can you approve?
kevin: approved :thumbsup:
sara: approved :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: approval threshold met. scheduling deployment.
ops-bot: reminder: keep on-call engineer looped: @chris will be on-call for the window.
chris: on-call and will watch p95 + 500ms tail. I'll jump in if anything looks off.
anna: small checklist before start:
- confirm pinned versions (done)
- release notes in ticket (done)
- probes added (done)
- approvers (done)
- oncall confirmed (done)

anna: when I kick off I'll post the rollout commands. quick reference:
```
# kick
deploy-bot trigger router-weighted-shift --config rtr-2026-03-slim --pin service:v2.3.1
# abort
deploy-bot abort router-weighted-shift
```
kevin: can we set a 2-minute quiet period after each step to watch logs before next step? avoids noisy oscillations.
sara: 2m quiet period OK. add to plan.
chris: also enable temporary increased logging level for router1 during roll (debug for 15m) so we can capture root cause if needed.
anna: doing that in the pre-step. expected impact minimal.
deploy-bot: scheduled start at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z. notifier: #eng-releases and #incidents.
kevin: one more thing — pin the session affinity cookie TTL to 5m during the shift to reduce stickiness variance.
sara: noted, adding `session_ttl=300s` to config.
anna: final plan looks good. I'll kick at the window and post progress updates here. thanks everyone :rocket:
chris: thanks — will keep an eye and ready to revert.
deploy-bot: rollout started: step 1 -> 10% to router1
anna: Step 1 completed. probes green. moving to 50% in 12m.
ops-bot: automatic monitoring: p95 1.02x baseline, error_rate 0.6% — within thresholds.
kevin: good to proceed when you see stable traces.
anna: moving to 50% now.
chris: logs show slight uptick in kv_cache_miss at t+3m, but hit rate recovered by t+6m. still fine.
anna: moving to 100% in 8m if no regressions.
kevin: confirm rollback hooks ready? just say the word.
sara: all rollback hooks set. remember abort syntax in ticket.
anna: 100% applied. probes green for 10m. router1 handling traffic.
deploy-bot: rollout complete. marking deployment as success.
anna: updating release ticket with final metrics and closing window. great job everyone.
chris: leaving a quick postmortem note: watch kv cache warmup on the next few shifts, might be worth pre-warming for larger models.
kevin: adding prewarm task to backlog.
anna: closing thread. :tada:
